name: Self-Compassion
intro: Welcome. Today, the kindness is directed inward.
We're so good at caring for others. So practiced at putting ourselves last.
Right now, you are the one who gets the care.
Not because you earned it. Not because you deserve it more than yesterday.
But because you are a living being, and that is enough.
body: Think of how you speak to yourself when you make a mistake.
The tone. The words. Would you use them on someone you love?
Most of us speak to ourselves in ways we'd never speak to a friend.
What if, starting now, you treated yourself like someone worth being kind to?
Because you are.
Place your hand over your heart.
Feel its beat. Steady. Faithful. Yours.
Say silently to yourself: I am doing my best.
Even if your best today looks different from your best yesterday.
It still counts. It always counts.
Think of something you've been criticizing yourself for.
Now imagine a child came to you with the same struggle.
What would you tell them? Would you call them stupid? Lazy? Worthless?
Or would you kneel down, look them in the eyes, and say: It's okay. You're learning.
Now say that to yourself. Mean it.
You are allowed to be imperfect.
Perfection was never the goal. It was the cage.
What if your cracks are not flaws but openings? Places where light gets in.
Every scar you carry is proof that you healed from something.
You are not broken. You are weathered. And weathered things have character.
Repeat these words in your mind, slowly.
May I be kind to myself.
May I accept myself as I am.
May I forgive myself for what I didn't know.
May I remember that I am enough.
Let those words settle. Not as wishes. As truths.
closing: Self-compassion is not selfish. It's the foundation of everything.
You can't pour from an empty cup. And you've been pouring for a long time.
Today, you refilled just a little. That matters.
Take a deep breath. You are worthy of your own kindness.
Open your eyes. And carry that warmth with you.
